segments.name: Mobile Bay Lateral Expansion Phase 1, 30-inch onshore and Mobile Bay segment

start.description: Existing Transco Compressor Station 82 (Coden, Mobile County, Alabama, on the Mobile Bay shore)

end.description: New offshore connection platform in Mobile Block 822 (junction platform)

segments.name: Mobile Bay Lateral Expansion Phase 1, 24-inch offshore segment

end.description: New platform in Main Pass / Viosca Knoll Block 261 (NGI calls it East Main Pass 261, near the edge of the outer continental shelf)

refs.quote: 19.08 miles of 30-inch-diameter pipeline from existing compressor station 82 in Mobile County, Alabama to a new offshore connection platform in Mobile Block 822 (this segment involves approximately 4.00 miles of onshore pipeline); 56.58 miles of 24-inch-diameter pipeline from the new offshore connection platform in Mobile Block 822 to a new platform in Main Pass Viosca Knoll Block 261

P8284.notes: The 1997 FERC notice says only about 4.00 mi of the 30-inch segment is onshore, so the pipe leaves Compressor Station 82 at Coden, crosses the shore and runs about 15 mi through Mobile Bay water to the Block 822 platform. No source I could read states coordinates for Station 82, the landfall, Block 822 or Block 261. Block coordinates need the BOEM or BSEE block outlines and platform or pipeline segment data, which I did not reach (BOEM segment number not found). The same notice also lists 15,000 hp more at Station 82 and a new Compressor Station 83 in Mobile County. Whether the new pipe loops the original Mobile Bay Lateral is not stated in any source I read; trade press (NGI, via search results only, page not read) describes it as an offshore extension that adds capacity on the existing lateral. A Norphlet 16-inch gathering line later tied in at the Main Pass 261A junction platform. EIA's historical list shows this project as Transco Mobile Bay Lat Expansion I, docket CP97-92, 76 mi, completed August 1998.

start.description: Receipt meter station near Pascagoula at the terminus of the Gulf LNG Pipeline, Bayou Casotte area of the Port of Pascagula

end.description: Tie-in with the existing Mobile Bay Lateral near Grand Bay, Alabama (the tie-in is also the start of FGT's 8.8 mi Mobile Bay Lateral Extension, which runs to FGT Compressor Station 44)

refs.quote: Approximately 15.5 miles of 26-inch-diameter jointly owned pipeline from Jackson County, Mississippi to Grand Bay, Mobile County, Alabama; ... A receipt meter station near Pascagoula in Jackson County, Mississippi
about 15 miles of 26-inch-diameter pipeline extending from this receipt point interconnect to FGT's and Transco's existing Mobile Bay Lateral in Mobile County, Alabama (Pascagoula Supply Line)
a greenfield natural gas pipeline connecting the Gulf LNG Pipeline with Applicants' existing Mobile Bay Lateral

P8229.notes: Direction of the pipe: it starts in Jackson County, Mississippi and runs east into Mobile County, Alabama, ending at Grand Bay, Alabama, where it meets the Mobile Bay Lateral. No milepost on the Mobile Bay Lateral and no coordinates were found in the Federal Register notices. The two notices split the mileage as about 4.45 mi in Mobile County and 10.85 mi in Jackson County (from the search summary of a Federal Register notice, not read in full). Maps are in Appendix 1 of the 2008 notice and in the FERC environmental assessment, both on eLibrary (docket CP09-456; PF08-31 and PF08-32), which I could not download. Also stated: the notice says Compressor Station 82 would be modified.

segments.name: Sabine Pass Compression Project tie-in facility (36-inch tap)

start.description: New tie-in facility next to Natural's existing tap on its lateral to the Sabine Pass LNG Terminal

end.description: New compressor station on Natural's Louisiana Line Nos. 1 and 2, adjacent to the Sabine Pass LNG Terminal

refs.quote: a new compressor station with a 22,490-horsepower natural gas-fired Solar Titan 130 turbine compressor unit ... along Natural's existing Louisiana Line Nos. 1 and 2, adjacent to the Sabine Pass LNG Terminal; and a new tie-in facility ... four 30-inch taps ... and a 36-inch tap on Natural's existing lateral pipeline to the Sabine Pass LNG Terminal
Sabine Pass Compression Project ... facilities by Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America, LLC (Natural) in Cameron Parish, Louisiana

P2607.notes: Likely mis-attributed owner. I found no Transco project called Sabine Pass Compression Expansion. The match is Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America's Sabine Pass Compression Project, FERC docket CP18-487-000 (order issued September 30, 2019), in Cameron Parish, Louisiana. EIA lists it as completed October 2020 with a 36-inch diameter, which matches GEM's 2020 start and 36-inch diameter, but the owner on the sheet is Transco. No pipeline length is stated in the order: the new pipe is only a short tie-in with suction lines at an existing tap, so 0.48 km (about 0.3 mi) is plausible but not confirmed by a source. No coordinates found. A Transco project that does touch Sabine Pass is Gulf Trace (docket CP15-29, about 6.97 mi of 36-inch lateral in Cameron Parish plus Compressor Station 44 units, service 2017), which is not 2020 and not 0.48 km; I did not read a primary source for it. Recommend a person confirm owner and docket before any route is drawn. A route for 0.3 mi of tie-in pipe inside an LNG terminal tie-in is probably not worth building.

start.description: Transco mainline at Compressor Station 115 area

end.description: Carroll County, Georgia (continues as 24-inch; Compressor Station 116 is new in Carroll County)
Bartow County, Georgia (new meter station in Bartow County)

refs.quote: about 113 miles of new natural gas pipeline and associated facilities in Coweta, Carroll, Douglas, Paulding, Bartow, Gordon, and Murray Counties, Georgia ... about 7.6 miles of new 30-inch-diameter pipeline in Coweta and Carroll Counties ... 48.2 miles of new 24-inch-diameter pipeline in Carroll, Douglas, Paulding, and Bartow Counties ... 53.5 miles of new 20-inch-diameter pipeline in Bartow, Gordon, and Murray Counties ... 1.5 miles of new 16-inch-diameter pipeline in Murray County
approximately 111.2 miles of new pipeline and install a new 21,830 horsepower compressor station in Carroll County, Georgia
Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company, LLC's (Transco's) Dalton Expansion Project ... new pipeline and aboveground facilities in Georgia

P8279.notes: The county order is Coweta, Carroll, Douglas, Paulding, Bartow, Gordon, Murray. The mileage by diameter sums to 110.8 mi; the notice says about 113 mi, and EIA and press say 111 to 115 mi. The segment boundaries within counties are inferred from the county lists and are not stated. Search summaries (not read in full) say the lateral begins at Transco's Compressor Station 115 in Coweta County and a 2.0 mi AGL Spur of 16-inch connects to the Murray meter station; the three new meter stations are in Bartow and Murray Counties. EIA's current release says the lateral transfer point is near Compressor Station 115 and the terminus is near milepost 113 in Murray County. No downloadable route map or GIS was reached: the FERC EA and its alignment sheets are on eLibrary (docket CP15-117, pre-filing PF14-10) and the scoping notice's maps are in the FERC file. University of Georgia archaeology reports (archaeology.uga.edu) for the project carry route figures but were not read. No coordinates found.

start.description: Existing Moore Compressor Station and the Transco-Moore receipt point

end.description: Chappells (Greenwood County, near the Greenwood Town Border Station)

refs.quote: Approximately 55 miles of 12-inch-diameter pipeline in Spartanburg, Laurens, Newberry, and Greenwood Counties (Moore to Chappells Pipeline); approximately 5 miles of 4-inch-diameter pipeline in Dillon County (Dillon Pipeline); installation of two new 1,400-horsepower (hp) compressor units at the existing Moore Compressor Station in Spartanburg County
Aiken, Charleston, Dillon, Dorchester, Greenwood, Laurens, Newberry, and Spartanburg Counties, South Carolina (Transco to Charleston Project)

P4382.notes: FERC docket CP16-98-000 (pre-filing PF15-29), applicant Dominion Carolina Gas Transmission, LLC, filed March 9, 2016. The 55 mi that GEM records is the Moore to Chappells Pipeline, 12-inch, running through Spartanburg, Laurens, Newberry and Greenwood Counties, from the Moore Compressor Station area where gas enters from Transco to Chappells. The 5 mi 4-inch Dillon pipeline is a separate small line. The route follows the Moore to Chappells corridor in Spartanburg, Laurens, Newberry and Greenwood counties; the Chappells end point is my reading of the name and the Greenwood Town Border Station upgrade, not a stated end point. A SC DES public notice (https://des.sc.gov/sites/des/files/docs/HomeAndEnvironment/Docs/Dominionpublicnotice.pdf) and the FERC EA on eLibrary likely hold route maps; I did not read them. No coordinates found.

start.description: Existing Virginia Natural Gas transmission system near Quantico

end.description: New interconnect station with Transco near Catlett, Virginia; the proposed compressor station was on Nokesville Road near the Transco crossing

refs.quote: 6.2 miles of 30-inch-diameter steel pipeline extending north from VNG's existing natural gas transmission system located near Quantico. It would run through Fauquier and Prince William counties and connect with the Transco pipeline via an interconnect station located near Catlett. The company is also seeking to construct another 3.3 miles of 30-inch diameter steel pipeline running parallel to the company's existing pipeline in Fauquier County.
approximately 9.5 miles of pipeline ... nearly all adjacent to existing energy infrastructure in utility corridors

P3200.notes: Virginia Natural Gas filed with the Virginia State Corporation Commission on December 6, 2019 (the press-release page speaks of a proposed in-service date of December 2023; the news article says December 31, 2022). SCC case number PUR-2020-00283 is from a search summary and was not verified. The 10 mi in GEM is the 6.2 + 3.3 = 9.5 mi total. The route runs along existing utility corridors, so the route can be traced next to the Transco pipeline and VNG's existing line between Quantico and Catlett. No coordinates or route map were found; the VNG application PDF link from search results is dead (404). Cancellation: I did not find the withdrawal order; one search summary pointed to a March 2021 news item on VNG withdrawing the application, not verified.
